data.long_meaning: The name Harmesh is derived from the Sanskrit language and is a compound of two words: Haram (God's) andesh (treasure). This name signifies that the person is a treasure given by God and is held in high esteem. The name Harmesh carries the meaning “God's treasure” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Harmesh usually hope their child will grow to embody god's treasure and live with faith, good character and purpose.

vedic_reference.note: The name Harmesh is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Rama' and 'Ish' (meaning 'God'). It is a name of Lord Rama in Hinduism, who is an avatar of Vishnu and is known for his virtues, courage, and righteousness. In Hindu mythology, Rama is considered to be the ideal man and the embodiment of dharma. The name Harmesh can also be considered a name of Lord Shiva, as 'Ish' is also a common epithet of Shiva.

historical_references.reference: The Hindu monarch Harmesh was the ruler of the small principality of Malwa, in central India, during the 15th century. He is best known for his patronage of the poet Alha Bharati, who composed a series of epic poems in Sanskrit that celebrated the goddess Durga and the hero Alha.

Harmesh, also known as Harihara, was a Jain monarch who ruled the kingdom of Gujarat in the 14th century. He is revered for his strict adherence to Jainism and his efforts to establish religious harmony between Hindus and Jains in his kingdom.
